title: Interpret How Generic Robot Commands Are Translated to Vendor REST API via Geek Plus COM Module
summary: Use the Robot Command Database model command names to understand how OptiSweep’s Robotics module issues generic internal robot commands to the Geek Plus COM module, and how that COM module translates those vendor-agnostic commands into the vendor-specific REST API POST requests (then converts responses back to what OptiSweep expects). This supports vendor-agnostic command modeling and helps interpret why command names remain generic.
when_to_use: When you need to interpret the vendor-agnostic internal robot command model (generic command names) and understand the translation layer that produces vendor REST API POST requests via the Geek Plus COM module.
not_for: Do not use this runbook to verify a specific vendor REST endpoint URL, request payload fields, or response schema—those details are not provided in the source packet.
roles_and_responsibilities: L2_support: Interpret the Robot Command Database model command names and map them to the described translation path (Robotics module -> Geek Plus COM module -> vendor REST API POST request).
access_or_tools_needed: Robot Command Database model table view (RobotCommandDatabaseModel) showing generic command names

visual_references.description: RobotCommandDatabaseModel command names list (e.g., EmptyGoTo, PickupTote, MoveTote, DropOffTote, RemoveAgv, ReleaseAgv, GoCharge) and description that these are generic internal commands translated by Geek Plus COM module into REST API POST requests.

WCS creates several databases; OptiSweep only utilizes entity logs for logging; includes context about debugging/logging and related database models (Audit Geek, OPC Comms, Robotics, Sworder Sweeper).

steps.purpose: Identify the generic internal robot command names that the Robotics module issues and that the Geek Plus COM module translates.
steps.instruction: Open the Robot Command Database model table view (RobotCommandDatabaseModel) and review the listed generic command names shown in the artifact (e.g., EmptyGoTo, PickupTote, MoveTote, DropOffTote, RemoveAgv, ReleaseAgv, GoCharge).

steps.title: Confirm the commands are internal/generic (not vendor-specific)

steps.instruction: Using the source description, confirm that the RobotCommandDatabaseModel commands are described as generic internal commands between the Robotics module and the Geek Plus COM module (and that a different vendor would use a different translation module while keeping the internal command model generic).
steps.expected_result: You can state (based on the source) that these commands are “very generic” and “not vendor specific,” and that the Geek Plus COM module translates them into the vendor REST API POST requests.

steps.title: Interpret the translation path to vendor REST API POST requests
steps.purpose: Explain how the internal command model results in vendor-specific REST API POST requests via the Geek Plus COM module.
steps.instruction: Using the source description, interpret the translation path as: Robotics module issues generic internal commands -> Geek Plus COM module translates them into the actual vendor REST API POST request -> Geek Plus COM module converts it back to the way OptiSweep expects.
steps.expected_result: You can correctly describe the translation layer: Geek Plus COM module is the component that translates internal generic commands into the vendor REST API POST request (and then converts responses back to OptiSweep’s expected format).
steps.healthy_condition: Your interpretation aligns with the source statement that the Geek Plus COM module translates internal commands into the actual REST API POST request and supports vendor-agnostic modeling.
steps.failure_condition: You assume the Robotics module directly calls the vendor REST API POST request (the source attributes translation to the Geek Plus COM module).

actions.label: Map internal command to translation layer
